title: SubscriberCharge
description: One charge in a subscriber's account: an amount that became due for a period, derived from a line of the contract in force. The journal is append-only — a charge is never updated, and a mistake is answered with a counter-entry rather than an edit, so the account says what happened rather than what somebody thinks today. A charge is net: the tax is decided by the tax adapter when the charge is invoiced, from the subscriber's origin on that day, and computed once per rate on the invoice.

then.description: A correction names what it corrects and moves it by an amount, towards nothing.

else.description: Every other charge names nothing it corrects.

id.description: The charge's own identifier. Never shown to a customer as an invoice number: invoice numbering is sequential, gapless and legally constrained per country, and an identifier somebody has already seen on a screen cannot become one later without confusion.

subscriberId.description: The party the contract is concluded with, whose account this is. It outlives the tenant.

tenantId.description: The tenant the subscription belonged to when the charge arose.

subscriptionId.description: The subscription the charge arose on. Part of the natural key.

contractId.description: The contract whose line the charge realises.

contractLineItemId.description: The contract line the charge came from, so that every invoice line can be traced back to what was agreed.

sourceRef.description: Which thing of its source the charge is for, stable across contracts: the subscription id for the plan, the booking id for an add-on, the discount's key for a discount — and for a correction, the invoice it was corrected on and the charge it corrects, `<invoiceId>/<chargeId>`, so that each correction is an entry of its own. Part of the natural key (subscriptionId, source, sourceRef, periodStart, origin), which is unique — a charge derived twice is written once.

periodStart.description: The start of the period the charge belongs to — the grouping key for an invoice.

currency.description: ISO 4217, as the contract line records it — recorded per charge so that a charge written in 2026 still means what it meant after the configured currency changes.

amountNet.description: Net, rounded to the currency's decimal places once, when the charge is written; the written figure is the truth from then on. Negative for a discount and a credit; a correction has the sign that moves its charge towards nothing — negative for a charge that asks, positive for a discount.

bookedAt.description: When the amount became due. The account is ordered by this, not by when the row was written.

correction.description: On a correction, what it corrects and why; null on every other charge.

SubscriberChargeOrigin.description: What made the charge arise. activation: the first period of a subscription. renewal: a later period. planChange: what an immediate plan change adds. bundleBooking: the first, short period of an add-on. bundleChange: what an add-on's switch to a dearer version adds for the rest of its period. credit: a decision that reduces what is owed. correction: a counter-entry by which what an earlier charge asks falls, in whole or in part, which is how the append-only journal answers a mistake; only the cancellation of the invoice the charge stood on writes one, and only that cancellation's replacement invoices it. reductionTakenBack: a reduction granted in advance, taken back for the days it no longer covers — the feature it was granted for came back, or what it reduced ended at once.

SubscriberChargeCorrection.description: What a counter-entry corrects: a charge that stood on an invoice cancelled because the charge was not owed, or not in full. The counter-entry carries the corrected charge's contract line, source and period, and the amount by which what is owed falls.

chargeId.description: The charge it corrects. Never a correction: a counter-entry is not corrected in turn, the charge it corrects is.

invoiceId.description: The invoice the charge stood on when it was corrected, the one cancelled.

reason.description: Why, as the cancellation gave it; something besides blanks.

SubscriberChargeSource.description: Which kind of contract line the charge realises.
